title: Power torsion depends only on the closed subset: a module is I-power torsion exactly when its support lies in V(I)
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a ring R with a finitely generated ideal I, the subcategory of I-power torsion modules depends only on the closed subset Z = V(I) of Spec(R), and that a module is I-power torsion exactly when its support is contained in Z (statement lines 24085-24092). The proof is an elementwise computation that has to go through the localizations twice: an element annihilated by a power of I dies in the localizations at the elements of I and hence at the primes outside V(I), while conversely vanishing at all those primes must be lifted back to vanishing at the finitely many localizations M_{f_i}, which is where the finite generation of I is used, and only then do the annihilating exponents appear (proof lines 24095-24101). The last line identifies the power torsion submodule as the kernel of the map to the product of the localizations outside Z, and the dependence on the closed set rather than on the ideal follows from that description. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.
